title: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 vs GPT-5.6 Sol on DeepSWE: Cost, Coding, and Routing
gist: On the DeepSWE software-engineering benchmark, GPT-5.6 Sol wins single-shot accuracy (72.7% pass@1) while DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 costs 35x less ($0.24 vs $8.37 per rollout) and overtakes at pass@4 (88.5% vs 85.8%). Together AI argues the optimal play is a cascade running cheap Pro first and escalating to Sol only on test failures, hitting 83.0% at $3.35 per task, ten points better than Sol alone for 60% less.

insights.claim: Running DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 first and escalating to GPT-5.6 Sol only when tests fail solves 83.0% of DeepSWE tasks at $3.35 each, ten points above Sol alone (72.7%) and roughly 60% cheaper than Sol's $8.37 per task.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: A verifiable-domain cascade beats either model alone on both accuracy and cost, the central actionable takeaway.
insights.quote: Don't pick one. Run DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 first, escalate to GPT-5.6 Sol when the tests fail. That cascade solves 83.0% of DeepSWE tasks at $3.35 each.

insights.claim: The Pro-to-Sol cascade even beats a perfect one-shot oracle router (80.8%) because two independent attempts beat one perfect pick.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Counterintuitively, cheap sequential retries outperform even ideal model selection, favoring cascades over routers.
insights.quote: The cascade even beats a perfect one-shot oracle router (80.8%), because two independent attempts beat one perfect pick.

insights.claim: Accuracy is identical whichever model leads the cascade, but Pro-first costs $3.35 versus Fable-first-style $8.44, so you should always lead with the lower-cost model.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Ordering the cheap model first is a free cost saving with no accuracy penalty.
insights.quote: Accuracy is the same whichever model leads, but Pro-first is far cheaper ($3.35 vs $8.44), so always lead with the lower-cost model.

insights.claim: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 costs $0.24 per rollout versus GPT-5.6 Sol's $8.37, a 35x price gap that in value terms is 260 solves per $100 for Pro against 9 for Sol.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: A 35x cost differential reframes model choice around budget and throughput, not just accuracy.
insights.quote: Per $100 spent, Pro solves 261 tasks and Sol solves 9.

insights.claim: Sol does not buy speed or brevity with its price: Pro takes a median 146 steps, 35 minutes, and 101k output tokens versus Sol's 53 steps, 17 minutes, and 59k tokens.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Sol's premium is justified by latency and concision when a human is waiting, but never on budget or queue depth.
insights.quote: If a human is waiting, Sol earns its premium on latency alone; if a budget or a queue is waiting, nothing here is close to Pro.

insights.claim: GPT-5.6 Sol wins single-shot at 72.7% pass@1 vs Pro's 62.8% and holds the lead at pass@2 (81.0% vs 78.5%), but the gap inverts at pass@4 where Pro reaches 88.5% vs Sol's 85.8%.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: For best-of-k workloads the accuracy argument for Sol largely disappears, favoring cheap retries.
insights.quote: If your workload lets you run best-of-k, the accuracy argument for Sol largely disappears.

insights.claim: Decomposing pass@1, Sol is the precision corner with 84.5% reliability and 61 tasks solved four-for-four, while Pro trades to wider coverage (88.5% vs 85.8%) but lower reliability (71.0%) and only 35 solid tasks.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: The coverage-vs-reliability split explains the pass@4 crossover and guides which model to trust per shot.

insights.claim: Sol breaks the repository's existing test suite in 20% of its failures, the GPT-family regression signature, versus 11% for the more conservative Pro whose failures are usually near-misses with the baseline intact.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Sol's diffs need a full regression gate before acceptance, adding a hidden cost to its output.
insights.quote: put a full regression gate around Sol before you take its diff, and Pro needs that guardrail less.

insights.claim: Sol wins 6 of 8 task domains, led by data modeling and serialization at 92% (28 points over Pro), while Pro's only domain win is stateful reactivity (66 vs 64) and language/runtime internals is a 75-75 tie.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Exact-contract serialization work is where Sol's premium is clearly earned.
insights.locator: Where each wins, by task type

insights.claim: Sol sweeps four of five languages (Python 74, Go 79, TypeScript 66, JavaScript 75) with wide Python and Go margins, but Pro wins Rust outright 65 to 60, the one language Sol underperforms.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Stack language dictates the pick: Python/Go favor Sol, Rust favors the far cheaper Pro.

insights.claim: The two models have per-task correlation of 0.54, both solve 90 tasks, Pro alone gets 10 and Sol alone gets 7, and their union covers 107 of 113 tasks (94.7%).
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Moderate disagreement and near-total union coverage are what make a two-model portfolio worthwhile.

insights.claim: Pro sweeps no task that Sol misses entirely, while Sol goes four-for-four on two tasks Pro never solves, so Pro adds little new reach but adds the ability to clear shared tasks at minimal cost.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Pro's value in the pair is cost reduction on shared tasks, not expanding the solvable set.

insights.claim: GPT-5.6 Sol is the single-model pick when correctness and latency both matter on the first try, but buyers pay 35x Pro's cost and must guardrail its 20% regression rate.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: Clarifies when the flagship premium is defensible versus when Pro or the cascade wins.

insights.claim: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 is the value and best-of-k pick with near-flagship coverage, the higher four-shot ceiling, and a cleaner failure profile at $0.24 a rollout.
insights.speaker: Zain Hasan, Shobhit Dixit
insights.so_what: For high-volume or retry-tolerant agent work, Pro is the stronger value pick.
